title: G2: Sufficiency of pentagon/hexagon-local conditions for global geodeticity

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap G2 (deepest).** Necessity of the cycle-local conditions is comparatively easy; SUFFICIENCY is the analytic core. Must show: if every 5-cycle and 6-cycle of $H$ satisfies its arc conditions, then EVERY pair of vertices of $G'$ has a unique shortest path -- including pairs whose geodesic leaves any single cycle and threads through several pentagons/hexagons.

Suggested route: use that $H$ has diameter 2 and girth 5 (Moore graph). Any two branch vertices are at $H$-distance $\le2$; any geodesic in $G'$ between branch vertices uses paths of at most 2 original edges plus possibly a length-2 detour via a common neighbour. Enumerate these finitely many configurations and show each lies inside some pentagon or hexagon -- this is precisely why only 5- and 6-cycles appear. For pairs where one/both endpoints are interior (degree-2) vertices, reduce to the branch-vertex case along the subdividing path.

This sufficiency lemma is what turns the necessary system into an equivalence.
